Scan an R serialization file for code and references

Source: R/scan.R
rds_scan.Rd

Reports everything in a file that can run code when the file is loaded or used, that reaches outside the file, or that needs a package to load, without loading it. Nothing in the file is evaluated, and a file R itself would refuse can still be scanned.

Usage

rds_scan(x, kind = NULL)

rds_is_safe(x, kind = NULL)

Arguments

x

A path, a raw vector (a serialize() result, or a file's bytes) or a connection open for reading in binary mode. For a lazy-load database, the path without extension, as lazyLoad() takes it, or the path of its .rdb or .rdx file.

kind

NULL to detect the kind of file, or one of "rds", "rda" and "lazyload" to insist on it.

Value

For rds_scan(), a data frame with one row per finding, in stream order:

  • path: where in the object, such as [[2]]$fit (see zurds-conditions for the notation); "" for the object itself, and $name for an object of an .rda.

  • finding: "closure", "promise", "bytecode", "environment", "external_pointer", "weak_reference", "namespace", "package_environment", "persistent_reference", "altrep" or "s4".

  • detail: the namespace or package environment, the ALTREP class and its package, or the S4 class and its package; NA otherwise.

  • severity: "executes" (closures, promises, bytecode), "reaches_out" (environments, namespaces, package environments, external pointers, weak and persistent references) or "needs_package" (ALTREP and S4).

For rds_is_safe(), TRUE when rds_scan() finds nothing.

Details

Base R's own ALTREP classes (compact sequences such as 1:10, deferred strings and wrappers) need no package and are read by rds_read_data(); they are not findings.

The scan is advisory for readRDS(): a clean scan means the file holds no type that can run code when it is loaded, but readRDS() still creates objects of the file's classes, and using them can call methods you have loaded.

See also

Other safety: rds_deps()

Examples

rds_scan(system.file("extdata", "model.rds", package = "zurds"))
#>                                                                  path
#> 1                                            [[2]][[11]]$.Environment
#> 2       [[2]][[11]]$.Environment@hashtab[[11]]$fit[[11]]$.Environment
#> 3 [[2]][[11]]$.Environment@hashtab[[11]]$fit[[12]]$terms$.Environment
#> 4                                      [[2]][[12]]$terms$.Environment
#>       finding detail    severity
#> 1 environment   <NA> reaches_out
#> 2 environment   <NA> reaches_out
#> 3 environment   <NA> reaches_out
#> 4 environment   <NA> reaches_out
rds_is_safe(system.file("extdata", "iris.rds", package = "zurds"))
#> [1] TRUE

# A promise that would run system() when used:
promise <- system.file("extdata", "promise.rds", package = "zurds")
rds_scan(promise)
#>    path finding detail severity
#> 1 [[2]] promise   <NA> executes
rds_is_safe(promise)
#> [1] FALSE
